answer_question: What did reports describe about cancer incidence or cancer registry data?
caption: 1989-90: Prince Edward Island's health department describes its provincial tumour registry, fed by pathology reports from two hospitals and sending incidence data to Statistics Canada. 2006: an Alberta cancer report describes the Alberta Cancer Board's registry of all new primary cancers and cancer deaths in the province. Two provinces' registries, each in its own report; not one registry over time.

comparability.label: Related but describing different things
comparability.note: Both pages answer the question: each describes where a provincial cancer registry's data comes from. They are different registries in different provinces, sixteen years apart, so the pair shows two ways of keeping a registry, not a change in either one.

notes.reason: The caption framed two provinces' registries as a single contrast.
notes.text: Corrected. Until October 29, 2026 this caption ended "A small registry reporting up, a large one reporting out", a contrast drawn across two provinces that the pages do not make.

answer_question: What did drinking-water quality guidelines recommend about contaminants?
caption: 1984: the proceedings of a national conference on drinking water quality warn that conventional treatment cannot remove some contaminants and call for a safe drinking water act with enforceable standards. 2011: British Columbia's Provincial Health Officer reports how drinking water is sampled and tested in that province (catalogued 2012). A national proposal and one province's monitoring report.

comparability.label: Related but describing different things
comparability.note: The 1984 page is a proposal made at a national conference; the 2011 page describes monitoring in one province and refers to the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality. Neither page is itself the guidelines, and neither shows whether the proposed act was passed or what led to BC's program.

notes.reason: The caption invented continuity between a national proposal and one province's program.
notes.text: Corrected. Until October 29, 2026 this caption ended "A case for the law, then a monitoring program running", which implied the 1984 proposal led to British Columbia's program. Neither page says so.

answer_question: What did the Canada Communicable Disease Report describe about notifiable disease trends?
caption: 1985-86: an Alberta annual report (catalogued 1987) describes the province's notifiable-disease program: required case reports, advice to local health authorities, hospitals and physicians, and data sent on to Statistics Canada. 2009: a Canada Communicable Disease Report supplement says the Public Health Agency of Canada will publish annual national surveillance summaries. A provincial program and a national reporting plan, described in different years.

comparability.label: Related but describing different things
comparability.note: Only the 2009 page is from the Canada Communicable Disease Report; the 1985-86 page is an Alberta annual report. One describes a provincial program, the other a national reporting plan, so the pair cannot show how notifiable-disease reporting developed.

notes.reason: The caption invented continuity across jurisdictions.
notes.text: Corrected. Until October 29, 2026 this caption ended "A provincial watch, then a national one", which read one province's program and a later national plan as a single succession. The two pages describe different programs in different jurisdictions.
